first_impression.reaction: I typed the search half expecting a mushy 'love is love' page with a rainbow banner. Instead the first word is 'Yes.', then the law, the date and the fact it's civil. Then it lists the three things I actually care about: 'Which documents you need, where the ceremony can take place, and whether the marriage counts when you fly home.' That's exactly my list. No 'fairytale', no 'dream day'. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Yes. As at November 2026, same-sex marriage in Greece is legal: Greek law allows a civil marriage between two persons of different or the same sex, and the change has been in force since 16 February 2024.
journey.reaction: A straight answer with a date and no fuss. I can forward this to Mum, who still thinks we'd have to go to Spain.

journey.section: Is same-sex marriage legal in Greece?
journey.quote: Article 1350 now reads: "Marriage is contracted between two persons of different or the same sex. Marriage requires the agreement of the intending spouses."
journey.reaction: Quoting the actual article and linking the law text is the lawyer in me getting what she wants. Not someone's blog summary of a blog summary.

journey.section: Civil ceremony at the town hall
journey.quote: On Rhodes, the Town Hall ceremony takes place every Wednesday and Friday, two adult witnesses over 18 must be present, and the couple returns to the registry office the next working day to sign and have the marriage certificate drawn up.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of detail only someone who's done it would flag. So a Friday wedding means we're signing on Monday? Good to know before half our guests book Sunday flights home.

journey.quote: Other islands may ask for more, or for less. Confirm the current list with the municipality where you will marry and with the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.
journey.reaction: Fair enough that it varies. But by this point I've been told to 'confirm with the municipality and the embassy' four or five times. 'Legal side sorted' is one of our three goals, and I still don't know whether that phone call is mine or my planner's.

journey.quote: DFAT can also issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask first whether yours must come from Athens and whether it needs an apostille.
journey.reaction: That's a real trap. We'd have happily got it done in Sydney and then found out it's the wrong one. Saved us a headache.

journey.section: Will your Greek marriage be recognised in Australia?
journey.quote: Your Greek marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not work as proof of a change of name, so check that with your state or territory registry of births, deaths and marriages.
journey.reaction: We've been going back and forth on whether one of us takes the other's name. Nobody mentioned this. Honest trade-off, plainly put.

journey.section: What the law covers, and what it does not
journey.quote: Couples declare their future children's surname before the wedding, to a notary or to the officiant, who must ask for it.
journey.reaction: We do want kids, and I'd never have guessed that's decided at the wedding in Greece. The 'easy to miss in the rush of a wedding week' line is exactly right.

journey.section: Is Greece LGBT friendly for a destination wedding?
journey.quote: Racially motivated and homophobic attacks have occurred.
journey.reaction: Stark, but I'd rather read it here than find out from a friend. It tells me they're not just selling me a sunset. The X passport line also tells me someone thought about couples who aren't us. Our older guests worry me more than we do, though.

journey.quote: Attitudes on Santorini are generally more accepting, as on Mykonos and Ios.
journey.reaction: After the Rhodes detail, Santorini and Mykonos are basically the Smartraveller line again plus a link. Those are the two islands our friends will assume we're picking, and I learn nothing new about doing the civil ceremony there.

journey.quote: In Lindos, the municipality lists St Paul's chapel platform, a tiny chapel below a cliff in the shadow of the Acropolis of Lindos, beside the turquoise water of St Paul's Bay.
journey.reaction: Now I can picture it. A legal ceremony there, not in a fluoro-lit office, is genuinely tempting.

journey.quote: Have you hosted same-sex weddings before, and will you put that in writing?
journey.reaction: Yes. This is the question we'd be too polite to ask and then regret. 'A venue that welcomes same-sex weddings will say so without hesitation' is exactly how we'd judge it.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around your civil ceremony, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing hit my currency and hidden-cost fears. But 'around your civil ceremony' reads like the paperwork itself stays with us. I'd want that spelt out.

journey.section: Legal ceremony, symbolic celebration or both
journey.quote: **Legal at home, celebration in Greece.** You marry in Australia first, then hold a symbolic ceremony at your Greek venue with no registry paperwork on the island.
journey.reaction: Honestly the option I'll be sending Jess. Three clear routes, no judgement on which is 'proper'. This is the bit that makes the decision feel manageable.

journey.section: Plan your Greece wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: The registrar settles the marriage. Everything around it, from the island and the venue to your guests' rooms and the long dinner after, is ours to plan.
journey.reaction: Clean line of who does what, and not schmaltzy. Still doesn't tell me whether they've done a wedding like ours before.

unanswered_questions: Does our Wedded Advisor chase the municipality and the embassy for us, or is the civil paperwork our job?
Have you planned a same-sex wedding in Greece before, and can we see one (venue and date)?
What do the Santorini and Mykonos municipalities actually ask for, and where will their registrars officiate?
If the Rhodes registrar only marries on Wednesdays and Fridays at the Town Hall, do the outdoor locations like Lindos follow the same days?
Can the civil ceremony be done in English, or do we need an interpreter for our guests?
How would you brief our older guests on the travel safety advice without frightening them?
would_share_with: Jess (partner): the intro, the three ways to shape the day, and the venue questions list
Mum and Dad (contributing): the recognition-in-Australia section, so they stop worrying it 'won't count'
Jess's parents: the 'Is Greece LGBT friendly' section, because they'll ask about safety first

cta_reaction.quote: When the legal route is clear, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=same-sex-marriage-greece&utm_content=primary) and plan the celebration around it.
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and telling me to sort the legal route first makes me trust it more. AUD quotes, one point of contact and the fee in writing address my hidden-cost and accountability fears. But I'd want to know they've done a same-sex wedding before and whether they help with the paperwork. I'd read the Santorini or Rhodes guide and look for a real wedding before I enquire.

top_3_changes: In 'Questions to ask a venue' or the closing section, after 'plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around your civil ceremony', say plainly whether the Wedded Advisor coordinates the municipality and embassy steps or whether the couple does them. The repeated 'Confirm with the municipality ... and the Australian Embassy' leaves the reader unsure who does the chasing.

In the 'Santorini' and 'Mykonos' subsections, add the civil ceremony detail the reader needs (what that municipality asks for and where its registrar officiates), or say plainly that it isn't published and goes on the booking checklist. At the moment both sections repeat 'Attitudes ... are generally more accepting' and link away, which feels thin next to Rhodes.

Near the closing CTA, add one confirmed line on whether Wedded Wonderland has planned same-sex weddings, and link a real one if there is one. Without it, 'Have you hosted same-sex weddings before, and will you put that in writing?' is the question I'd immediately turn back on the planner.
